precepts.text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel; that was the office before the Levites were taken instead.
precepts.point: The Levites were given as a gift to Aaron and to his sons, to do the service of the children of Israel and to make an atonement for them, that there be no plague among the children of Israel when they come nigh unto the sanctuary.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
Mark the word instead in verse 16: the Levites were taken “instead of such as open every womb, even instead of the firstborn of all the children of Israel.” At the first, the office belonged to all the firstborn of all the tribes. “And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.”

The firstborn were sanctified for the office from the day the Lord smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt. Here he makes it clear again, as he has done in multiple places, that the one tribe of Levi now performs the service of the tabernacle instead of them, given as a gift to Aaron and his sons to make an atonement for the children of Israel, that there be no plague when they come nigh unto the sanctuary.

precepts.text: The Levites were given to Aaron to do the service of the tabernacle and were set apart to this office.
precepts.point: He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and to make an atonement for the children of Israel: that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come nigh unto the sanctuary.” The Levites were given to Aaron to do the service of the tabernacle, set apart to this office.

That is why David declared, “None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath the Lord chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever.” He prepared a place for the ark in the city of David and pitched a tent for it, and this time he set it in the hands of those the Most High had chosen.

moments.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, This is it that belongeth unto the Levites: from twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: And from the age of fifty years they shall cease waiting upon the service thereof, and shall serve no more. Why at fifty? Because in the tabernacle you had to do heave offerings, where you had to lift the lamb, the goat, the bull or the ox up. That is the job of the twenty-five-year-old and up. At fifty God says they cease from that service.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: But shall minister with their brethren in the tabernacle of the congregation, to keep the charge, and shall do no service. So at fifty, what will they do? Minister with their brethren — in terms of teaching. No physical labour.
Thus shalt thou do unto the Levites touching their charge.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Aaron lighted the seven lamps to give light over against the candlestick, as the Lord commanded Moses; and the candlestick was of beaten gold, made according unto the pattern which the Lord had shewed Moses.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: The Levites were taken from among the children of Israel and cleansed: water of purifying sprinkled upon them, all their flesh shaven, and their clothes washed.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: The whole assembly of the children of Israel was gathered, the children of Israel put their hands upon the Levites, and Aaron offered the Levites before the Lord for an offering of the children of Israel, with the two bullocks for a sin offering and a burnt offering to make an atonement for the Levites.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: Thus were the Levites separated from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: After the cleansing the Levites went in to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Mark the word instead in verse 16: instead of such as open every womb, instead of the firstborn of all the children of Israel, the Most High took the Levites unto himself.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: At the first, all the firstborn of all the tribes were sanctified for the office, from the day the Lord smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt. Here he makes it clear again, as he has done in multiple places, that the one tribe of Levi now performs the service of the tabernacle.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: The Levites were given as a gift to Aaron and to his sons, to do the service of the children of Israel and to make an atonement for them, that there be no plague among the children of Israel when they come nigh unto the sanctuary.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: Moses, Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel did to the Levites according unto all that the Lord commanded Moses; the Levites were purified, and after that they went in to do their service in the tabernacle of the congregation before Aaron and before his sons.

note.label: Numbers 8: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

points: The service of the Levites had an age: from twenty and five years old and upward they went in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and up until that point they were not allowed to do the service.

From the age of fifty years they ceased waiting upon the service; it ran from twenty five to fifty. After fifty they ministered with their brethren in the tabernacle to keep the charge, but did no service.
